question: An archive keeps its films as data on tape. Why must it copy everything onto new tapes every few years?
answer: Because the machines die before the tapes. Each new generation of LTO data tape drive reads only tapes one or two generations older. A tape kept perfectly for twenty years can be unreadable simply because no working drive accepts it. Archives keep their collections alive by migrating them, again and again, on schedule.
move: Storing something is not keeping it if nothing can still read it.
ask: Which of my photos or files sit in a format I could no longer open?
reference: Ultrium LTO Program, LTO Generation Compatibility and Roadmap, 2021
